name: Prize crossword No 23,022
preamble: Most solutions contain an animal, which is ignored in the subsidiary part of the clue. Thus MAGNATE might be clued "Tycoon of the West (7)" (MA[GNAT]E). The rest (whose clues are asterisked) are normal.

clue.text: Since it's 10 off, take it for champagne

definitions.note: loose: the answer is an Italian sparkling wine, not true champagne

indicators.note: something that has gone off has turned bad, so these letters go wrong and come out in a new order

blocks.note: as in 'as you were out', meaning because
'tis, the poetic contraction of it is
the number written out as a word

explanation.surface: A bottle is ten per cent off, so you may as well pass it off as champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives ASTIS + NTE and ignores the animal PUMA, making ASTI SPUMANTE. '10' looks like a cross-reference to another clue but is just the number ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti spumante is a sweet sparkling white wine from Piedmont, often bought as a cheaper alternative to French fizz.

clue.text: Pupil has fruit drink

blocks.note: the apple of the eye is an old name for the pupil

explanation.surface: A schoolchild has a fruit drink at break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' wants to be a schoolchild; it is the apple of the eye. As the preamble says, the animal JACK, a male donkey, is left out of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Applejack is an American brandy distilled from cider, so a strong spirit made from orchard fruit.

clue.text: Alloy of lead and tin means end of bronze

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of bronze

explanation.surface: A metallurgy note: this lead-tin alloy marks the end of the bronze process.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says the wordplay ignores an animal: here TERN, a seabird, so only the E needs cluing.
explanation.definitionFit: Terne is a dull alloy, chiefly lead with some tin, used for coating sheet iron and steel.

clue.text: Sea duck on seafront

blocks.note: the front of sea is its first letter

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a sea duck bobbing just off the seafront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seafront' reads as one word but means the front of 'sea'. The animal left out of the wordplay is MEW, an old word for a gull.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small merganser, a diving duck that winters on coasts and estuaries.

clue.text: Get together with leaderless cue

indicators.note: without a leader means the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: cue without its opening C

explanation.surface: Players are told to come together, though nobody is leading the cue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is NIT, a louse's egg, which sits between the two letters the wordplay supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join or combine, the plain sense of coming together as one.

clue.text: The racecourse is like a little house

blocks.note: as in 'sly as a fox', meaning like
a cot is an old word for a small cottage

explanation.surface: Someone compares a grand racecourse to a cosy cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: One of the normal clues with no animal. ASCOT is the royal racecourse in Berkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is the famous English horse-racing venue, home of the Royal Ascot meeting each June.

clue.text: Notoriety's only part of the boxer

indicators.note: a portion of something is less than the whole, so just a stretch of letters is taken

blocks.note: the last letters of the first word run on into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A boxer's fame is mostly notoriety.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal clue. Mike Tyson, the heavyweight boxer, was notorious outside the ring, which makes the surface sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Tyson was the undisputed world heavyweight boxing champion of the late 1980s.

clue.text: It's incorrect to make the devil a cow-catcher

blocks.note: an imp is a little devil
one who ropes cattle

explanation.surface: It would be wrong to give Satan a job rounding up cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal clue. 'Cow-catcher' suggests the grille on a locomotive; here it is a cowboy with a lasso.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper means not in keeping with accepted standards, so wrong or unsuitable.

clue.text: The masterminder is his parent's child

blocks.note: Ma's, belonging to his mother
a male child

explanation.surface: A family note: the man behind it all is simply his parent's boy.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is GNU. Magnus Magnusson hosted the BBC quiz Mastermind, and his surname itself means 'son of Magnus'.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnus Magnusson was the long-serving presenter of Mastermind, the British television quiz show.

clue.text: Style of love and business

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like O
Co., short for company

explanation.surface: A firm's house style mixes romance with commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is ROC, the giant bird of Arabian legend, standing at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the ornate eighteenth-century decorative fashion of shells, scrolls and pastel curlicues.

clue.text: Help out with let in some way? I don't believe it!

indicators.note: done in some way or other, so the letters are put in an unspecified new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asked to lend a hand with letting a room doubts the story.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters rearrange to everything but HERON, the wading bird, which the wordplay ignores and which sits just before the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is short for 'pull the other leg, it's got bells on', a scoffing retort to a tall story.

clue.text: Screen devised for house

indicators.note: something devised is made up afresh, so the letters are worked into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A partition has been designed for a home.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is IDE, a freshwater fish, which splits the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a dwelling or home, especially a large or official one.

clue.text: A day early in the month - second to ninth and tenth, including fifth

definitions.text: A day early in the month

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for second
IX is nine in Roman numerals
taken as written
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A string of ordinals reads like someone dithering over which early date to pick.
explanation.walkthrough: Ninth and fifth are read as Roman numerals, and fifth goes inside tenth. The ignored animal is HORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names either of two dates in the first week, so a day early in any month.

clue.text: Proverbial reversal of plan for 1 ac

indicators.note: a reversal turns a word round to read the other way

blocks.note: a map is a plan of an area
the digit one looks like the letter I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cross-reference: swapping a plan around is proverbially the way to solve 1 Across.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 ac' looks like a pointer to 1 Across but is read literally, letter for letter. The ignored animal is ROE, a small deer, which splits the turned-round plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Paroemiac is a rare adjective from Greek paroimia, a proverb, so relating to or of the nature of sayings.

clue.text: Top of star cast

indicators.note: the top of a word is where it starts, so its first letter is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of star

explanation.surface: The headline name in a play's line-up of actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors; it is the verb to throw. The ignored animal is LING, a long fish of the cod family.
explanation.definitionFit: To sling something is to throw or hurl it carelessly, the same as casting it.

clue.text: Religious groups gas about November

indicators.note: to go about something is to surround it, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: CS gas is the tear gas used in riot control
ult., ultimo, means last month in old business letters, and November is last month when writing in December

explanation.surface: Sects spend November talking endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal clue with no animal. 'Gas' looks like the verb to chatter but is CS, the tear gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Cults are small religious sects, often devoted to a single leader or object of worship.

clue.text: River water container

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A jug filled from a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is EWE, a female sheep, so only the R needs cluing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large wide-mouthed jug, traditionally kept with a basin for washing.

clue.text: Scientist going forward

blocks.note: on as in 'go on', moving ahead

explanation.surface: A researcher making progress.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is NEWT, a small amphibian.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton was the English physicist and mathematician behind the laws of motion and gravitation.

clue.text: Turned out to be cut short

indicators.note: something put out of order is disarranged, so the letters land in a new sequence

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that seemed complete proved to be cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' reads as the phrase 'proved'; it is the fodder plus its anagram signal. The ignored animal is CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Truncated means shortened by having a part chopped off, typically the end.

clue.text: Swallowed a tablet? Ring the bell

blocks.note: to toll is to ring a bell slowly

explanation.surface: A patient swallows medicine, then rings for the nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is OKAPI, a forest relative of the giraffe, which splits the bell-ringing word in two.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the plain past tense of taking medicine in pill form, a tablet being a pill.

clue.text: Disorderly crew making new growth (for the old)

blocks.note: a rout is an old word for a disorderly crowd or rabble

explanation.surface: An unruly gang is somehow sprouting, and the parenthesis notes old-fashioned language.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is ASP, a venomous snake. '(For the old)' marks the answer as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Asprout is an old adverb or adjective meaning in the state of sprouting, like asleep or afloat.

clue.text: Health comes from playing "I spy" - hit on the head

indicators.note: playing with something means fiddling about with it, so the letters are moved around

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A child's guessing game is somehow good for you, until someone gets hit on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit on the head' looks like a phrase; 'hit' joins the fodder, and the head is NESS, a headland. The ignored animal is CALF.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical fitness is bodily good condition, the state of being strong and well.

clue.text: The setter's private

blocks.note: the setter speaking of themself: my

explanation.surface: The setter speaks of something personal to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective; it is the army rank. The ignored animal is TOM, a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tommy, from Tommy Atkins, is the traditional nickname for a British private soldier.

clue.text: Carver or composer, leader of society

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, which is the one kept

blocks.note: the first letter of society

explanation.surface: An artist, whether woodworker or musician, leads fashionable society.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is GIBBON, a small ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Grinling Gibbons was a celebrated woodcarver and Orlando Gibbons a Tudor composer, so the surname fits both.

clue.text: In the fashion of horoscopy, coincidentally with the sun when energy's lost

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so a letter drops out

blocks.note: heliacal describes a star rising or setting at the same time as the sun
E is the symbol for energy, and it is the letter dropped

explanation.surface: An astrologer describes a star rising with the sun just as the energy runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: HELIACALLY loses its E. The ignored animal is GENET, a spotted catlike carnivore.
explanation.definitionFit: Genethliacal means relating to birthdays or to casting nativities, the calculation of a birth chart.

clue.text: Military unit for man serving officer (Territorial Army)

indicators.note: one thing for another means it is swapped in, taking the other's place

blocks.note: a batman is an officer's personal servant in the army
TA is the abbreviation for the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A unit fit for an officer's servant, in the reservists.
explanation.walkthrough: TA replaces the MAN in BATMAN, giving BATTA. The ignored animal is LION, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is an army unit of several companies, forming part of a brigade.

clue.text: Pole has existed

blocks.note: N is the North Pole

explanation.surface: A Polish person has lived somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person; it is the north pole. The ignored animal is BEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Been is the past participle of to be, as in 'it has been', which is to have existed.

clue.text: Sedate at top of flight

blocks.note: staid means sober and sedate

explanation.surface: A calm passenger at the start of an air journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests aircraft; it is a flight of stairs. The ignored animal is RHEA, a flightless South American bird, sitting inside the word for sedate.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairhead is the landing at the upper end of a staircase, a flight being a run of steps.

clue.text: Taken heart with a boat

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so the middle letter is kept

blocks.note: the middle letter of taken
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone falls in love with a little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken heart' reads like being encouraged; it is the middle letter of 'taken'. The ignored animal is YAK, a long-haired ox.
explanation.definitionFit: A kayak is a narrow covered canoe, originally an Inuit craft of skins over a frame.

clue.text: Alien painter (not Claude)

blocks.note: ET, the extraterrestrial of the film

explanation.surface: An artist from another planet, who is not Claude.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is MAN, a joking choice since people are animals too. '(Not Claude)' steers away from Claude Monet to Édouard, a different painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Édouard Manet was the French painter of Olympia, often confused with Claude Monet.

clue.text: "Where'er you walk", maybe, dancing on legs

indicators.note: dancing feet move about, so the letters skip into another arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wherever you walk, you might as well dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is TIT, a small bird. 'Where'er you walk' is an aria from Handel's Semele, so its name is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted phrase is the name of a famous Handel aria, so it is an example of what a piece is called.

clue.text: Commercial for commercials: outside French Greenland Italian is English

indicators.note: to be outside something is to sit around it, so one part wraps the other

blocks.note: It. is the abbreviation for Italian
pays vert, green country in French, with the adjective after the noun
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An advertising slogan about a multinational: French, Greenlandic, Italian and English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greenland' looks like the island but splits into green + land, put into French. The ignored animal is TOAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The slogan is the advertising industry's pitch for its own services, so an advert for adverts.

clue.text: Chambers before printing?

blocks.note: MS, a manuscript, is the text as it stands before it goes to press

explanation.surface: A publisher's question: Chambers dictionary, before it goes to press?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chambers' looks like the dictionary publisher; it is plain rooms. The ignored animal is ROO, a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers are rooms, especially private or official ones such as a judge's or barrister's quarters.

clue.text: Protective armour for traditional post

blocks.note: chain mail is armour of linked rings

explanation.surface: A knight wants his armour delivered by ordinary post.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is SNAIL, which also explains the joke: a snail carries protective armour too.
explanation.definitionFit: Snail mail is the jokey name for letters sent through the postal service rather than by email.

clue.text: Two little boys in the dining room

definitions.note: describes where the answer stands rather than naming it

blocks.note: SID and ED, two short forms of boys' names

explanation.surface: Two small children are sitting in the dining room.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is BOAR, which sits between SID+E and D.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideboard is a long cabinet with drawers and cupboards, standard furniture for storing crockery near the table.

clue.text: Thou lovest Latin that can be collected

blocks.note: amas is Latin for 'thou lovest', from amo, amas, amat

explanation.surface: An affectionate declaration in Latin about something worth collecting.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is SABLE, a marten prized for its fur.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate, so the adjective describes things able to be gathered up.

clue.text: 1 - 0 for Welsh boy

blocks.note: the digit one looks like the letter I
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A one-nil scoreline for a Welsh lad.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 - 0' looks like a football score. The ignored animal ANT goes between I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ianto is a Welsh male name, a familiar form of Ifan, the Welsh John.

clue.text: Commotion helps to make 43 50

indicators.note: to help make something is to supply part of it, so just some letters are taken

blocks.note: the answers to 43 Down and 50 Across, side by side: the end of the first and start of the second

explanation.surface: A fuss contributes to a pair of other answers.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal clue: the letters straddle YAHOO and HANDOVERS, the answers at 43 and 50.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoo-ha is a fuss or noisy uproar, usually over something trivial.

clue.text: Posh member to take his seat for action against contract breaker

blocks.note: U means upper-class
a Member of Parliament
to sit is to take a seat

explanation.surface: A well-bred MP takes his seat in the Commons to sue someone who broke a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' and 'take his seat' suggest Parliament. The ignored animal is ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Assumpsit is an old common-law suit for damages over breach of a promise not under seal.

clue.text: Skilled/unskilled?

blocks.note: the surface reading: a word meaning able and expert
the setter's reading: the same word once doubled for its opposite, a foolish person

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure whether a worker counts as skilled or not.
explanation.walkthrough: DEFT means skilled, and it began as a variant of DAFT, now meaning foolish, from the same Old English word; the slash puts both senses in one entry. It also contains EFT, a newt.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft means nimble and neat-handed, the opposite of clumsy, while its old twin drifted towards silly.

clue.text: It sounds like a falcon, my poppet

indicators.note: how a thing sounds tells us to go by the spoken form, not the spelling

blocks.note: a lanner is a large falcon of Africa and southern Europe

explanation.surface: Someone tells their darling that their name rings like a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal clue. The answer is an Irish endearment, from Irish 'a leanbh', my child.
explanation.definitionFit: Alannah is an Irish term of endearment meaning my child, used like darling or pet.

clue.text: Examples attained after a time on board

definitions.text: attained after a time on board
definitions.note: describes the answer rather than naming it

blocks.note: e.g.s, plural of e.g., for example

explanation.surface: Examples that come with experience after some time aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is SEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea legs are the ability to keep balance on a moving ship, which sailors acquire after some days at sea.

clue.text: Attain heaven

blocks.note: to win something is to gain or attain it

explanation.surface: Reach paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is ELK, sitting inside the word for attain.
explanation.definitionFit: Welkin is a poetic old word for the sky or the vault of heaven.

clue.text: Brief article on old power station

blocks.note: terse means brief and to the point
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A short newspaper piece about a decommissioned power station.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is BAT. Battersea Power Station is the four-chimneyed landmark on the Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea Power Station in south London stopped generating electricity in 1983 and stood derelict for decades.

clue.text: School feature found by Alpine geologists

blocks.note: sch. is the abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: Mountain geologists on a school field trip spot something.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is FLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Flysch is a sequence of shales and sandstones, first described and named in the Swiss Alps.

clue.text: Heartless fun from playwright

indicators.note: with no heart a word loses its central letter

blocks.note: fun with its middle U taken away

explanation.surface: Joyless entertainment from a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is RAY, a flat fish. Michael Frayn wrote the farce Noises Off and the play Copenhagen.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Frayn is an English dramatist and novelist, best known for the backstage farce Noises Off.

clue.text: Lout raising crop circles

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising means lifting upward, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: hay is a crop grown for fodder
two rings, each shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A hooligan makes crop circles in a farmer's field.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal clue. 'Crop circles' reads as one thing but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A yahoo is a coarse brutish person, after the degraded humans in Gulliver's Travels.

clue.text: More or less nameless standard

blocks.note: c., circa, means approximately
anon., anonymous, without a name

explanation.surface: An approximately anonymous benchmark.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal clue with no animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a rule or criterion against which things are judged, as in canons of taste.

clue.text: Model car

blocks.note: the Model T was Ford's first mass-produced car

explanation.surface: A classic model car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Car' looks like a motor; it is a tramcar. The ignored animal is RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a streetcar running on rails, also called a tramcar, so a car of a kind.

clue.text: Old magistrate concerned with previous day

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
the eve is the day before

explanation.surface: A former judge is preoccupied with what happened yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal clue with no animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official in Anglo-Saxon England, a chief officer of a town or shire.

clue.text: Old magistrate, last of the line

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, which is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of line

explanation.surface: A former judge was the end of a dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is DOG.
explanation.definitionFit: The doge was the elected chief magistrate of the old republics of Venice and Genoa.

clue.text: A king at sea is vertical

blocks.note: taken as written
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A monarch adrift on the ocean stands upright.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is APE, at the front. 'At sea' looks like confusion; it labels the answer as a sailing term.
explanation.definitionFit: Apeak describes an anchor cable or oars held straight up and down, a sailor's word for upright.

clue.text: First papal seal

blocks.note: A is the first letter, and the top grade

explanation.surface: The very first seal a pope uses.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is BULL, which also names the papal document the seal is attached to.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulla is the round lead seal attached to a papal decree, which gave the bull its name.

clue.text: Transfers right into German boy

indicators.note: to go into something is to enter it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: Hans is a typical German boy's name
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A German lad's rights are passed on.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is DOVE, which goes inside the name alongside the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Handovers are acts of passing control or responsibility from one person to another.

clue.text: Dig up the dirt in the southeast, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means this is only one way things could go, so the letters may fall another way

blocks.note: taken as written
SE is the compass abbreviation for southeast

explanation.surface: A gossip digs up scandal about someone in the south-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: A normal clue with no animal. 'Dig up the dirt' is a tempting idiom, but only 'Dig up' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinter is to exhume, taking a buried body or object out of the ground.

clue.text: Girl with fellows has time for declaration

blocks.note: Ann is a girl's name
fellows are men
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A woman surrounded by men finally gets her moment to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: The ignored animal is OUNCE, the snow leopard, between the girl and the fellows.
explanation.definitionFit: An announcement is a public statement of news or intent, a formal declaration.
